Vary their scale and rotation.
Some float closer to the woman, some farther down toward the water.
They should feel playful and eerie rather than frightening.

LOWER SUPERNATURAL CREATURE:
Across the lower foreground, place one very large fox-like or feline supernatural creature lying horizontally on the edge of the dark water.

Its body is almost entirely dark:
black,
deep plum,
dark navy,
and burgundy.

Give it:
an extremely elongated body,
very large upright triangular ears,
long narrow muzzle,
half-closed glowing magenta eyes.

Decorate the face and body with restrained magenta-red ornamental markings.

The creature should occupy a long horizontal band across the lower composition, creating a strong counterweight to the vertical altar.

LOTUS AND SPIDER LILIES:
Place a glowing lotus-shaped ceremonial lamp near lower center-right.

The lotus should use saturated:
magenta,
hot pink,
coral red,
and warm orange at the inner core.

Hang a small rectangular yellow talisman beneath it.

Add several vivid pink-red spider lilies around the reclining creature:
one large bloom at lower-left,
one medium bloom near center,
one smaller flower toward viewer-right.

Keep the flowers stylized, constructed from thin graphic curved petals and radiating stamens.

WATER AND REFLECTIONS:
Use nearly black indigo water across the bottom.

Reflect the lotus, spider lilies and magenta accents using broken horizontal streaks rather than realistic mirror reflections.

The reflections should appear abstract and painterly but still cleanly controlled:
dark violet,
crimson,
magenta,
small cyan accents.

Do not create photorealistic ripples.

ANNOTATION SYSTEM:
Place multiple narrow red vertical seal-style labels next to the major figure and objects:
woman,
ritual vessel,
lantern,
ghost flames,
altar,
supernatural animal,
flowers.

Use thin red rectangular borders and vertical red Chinese characters.

Add one or two compact red square artist seals.

The annotation system should feel like a specimen diagram, mythological catalog or cultural poster rather than subtitles.

BOTTOM TYPOGRAPHY:
Along the bottom edge, arrange a restrained editorial credit strip.

Use small Latin typography, Chinese title text, a calligraphic signature-like mark and tiny secondary credits.
Keep the line thin and visually subordinate to the illustration.

COMPOSITION:
Maintain a very strong vertical hierarchy.

Upper third:
vast starry dark negative space.

Upper-middle:
giant ritual vessel + seated woman.

Center:
pale cyan stone bench.

Lower-middle:
extremely tall vertical stone shaft and cascading ribbons.

Bottom:
horizontal supernatural creature + glowing lotus + spider lilies + dark reflective water.

The woman remains the main human focal point.
The giant vessel forms the secondary vertical focal point.
The glowing lanterns create circular rhythm around the central structure.
The magenta flowers and fox create a bright lower anchor.

STYLE:
T1 flat 2D contemporary Chinese graphic illustration.
Modern Chinese editorial poster.
Oriental supernatural narrative design.
Geometric character anatomy.
Elongated stylized proportions.
Clean polygonal silhouettes.
Strong negative-space composition.
Selective gradients.
Decorative Art-Deco-like geometry.
Chinese folk religion and ghost-story motifs translated into contemporary visual design.
Subtle vintage lithographic and screen-print texture.
No thick cartoon outline.

COLOR ARCHITECTURE:
dominant dark field:
midnight blue,
black,
deep indigo,
cobalt.

central cool structure:
cyan,
turquoise,
ice blue,
pale mint.

skin:
pale lavender pink.

high-saturation accents:
magenta,
hot pink,
crimson,
violet.

practical-light accents:
ivory white,
pale pink,
tiny warm yellow.

LIGHTING ARCHITECTURE:
Unlike a daylight illustration, do not use one broad global light source.

The scene is primarily lit by several localized practical sources.

Lanterns:
soft warm-white and pale pink radial glow,
very soft edge,
limited radius.

Lotus lamp:
strong magenta-pink upward glow concentrated in the lower center.

Ambient night fill:
very low-intensity cool cobalt-blue fill from the environment.

Figure:
face and hands receive restrained cool cyan-blue illumination plus a faint warm pink contamination from nearby lanterns.
Shadow sides remain lavender, navy and deep violet.

Altar:
pale cyan top surfaces remain brightest;
vertical surfaces descend progressively into deeper cobalt and indigo.

Maintain deep shadow masses.
Do not lift the entire night scene.
No cinematic rim light.
No volumetric fog.
No bloom covering large areas.
Glows remain localized and graphic.

STYLE FIDELITY LOCK:
Preserve T1 flat 2D illustration.
Preserve angular elongated anatomy.
Preserve matte graphic planes.
Preserve the dark-blue nocturnal palette.
Preserve the cyan vertical altar.
Preserve magenta supernatural highlights.
Preserve localized lantern glow.
Preserve large areas of dark negative space.
Preserve subtle vintage paper texture.

Do not convert to photorealism.
Do not create realistic human skin.
Do not add pores.
Do not create realistic hair strands.
Do not create visible textile fibers.
Do not use glossy 3D CGI.
Do not turn the image into a game splash illustration.
Do not use generic anime faces.
Do not add excessive magical particles.
Do not add realistic fog.
Do not add horror gore.
Do not make the ghost spirits frightening monsters.
Do not replace the graphic fox with a realistic animal.
Do not over-brighten the night background.

assets.title: 夜城提灯的巨灵神女
assets.prompt:
Create a highly polished vertical 9:16 contemporary Chinese supernatural editorial poster that combines ancient Chinese deity imagery with a modern urban nightscape.

The image must remain unmistakably T1 flat 2D graphic illustration rather than realistic digital painting.

OVERALL COMPOSITION:
Build the entire poster around one monumental vertical figure.

The main supernatural woman occupies approximately the middle 65–70% of the frame width and almost the entire height between the upper-middle sky and the city skyline.

Her body forms the main central vertical axis.

Use three major visual scales:
1. gigantic main deity in the foreground-middle;
2. even larger but faint translucent cultural spirit silhouette behind her;
3. extremely small modern city buildings and people at the bottom.

This extreme scale difference is essential.

Keep the upper and side areas dark and spacious so the silhouette remains elegant rather than crowded.

BACKGROUND NIGHT SKY:
Use near-black at the extreme top and corners, gradually transitioning into saturated midnight navy, ultramarine and cobalt toward the lower half.

Scatter many extremely small stars across the upper background:
cold white,
pale cyan,
occasional electric-blue points.

Do not create a realistic Milky Way.
The stars should behave like sparse decorative print dots.

Overlay extremely subtle handmade-paper grain, faint pigment noise and vintage lithographic texture across the blue-black field.

Do not use smooth digital gradients without texture.

GHOSTLY BACKGROUND FIGURE:
Behind the main deity, create an enormous semi-transparent monochrome blue image of an ancient Chinese female musician, celestial maiden or mural-like cultural spirit.

The figure should be much larger than the foreground deity and only partially visible.

Show:
large head and shoulders,
traditional ancient hairstyle or headdress,
a long Chinese string instrument extending diagonally,
large sweeping robe masses,
calm monumental pose.

Render this background spirit almost entirely in:
deep royal blue,
cobalt,
electric blue,
and darker transparent indigo.

Its opacity should remain low enough that it feels embedded into the sky.

Do not outline it heavily.

Around this spectral figure, add:
thin plum blossom branches rising upward,
small blue flowers,
crescent-moon motifs,
faint stylized cloud ribbons,
subtle decorative stars.

These elements should feel like an enormous faded mural or ancestral memory floating behind the modern scene.

MAIN DEITY — BODY AND PROPORTIONS:
Place a gigantic elegant female deity in the center foreground.

Use highly elongated stylized proportions:
small head,
long neck,
narrow shoulders,
very long arms,
extremely long torso and robe silhouette,
thin delicate hands.

Her posture should feel relaxed, ritualized and self-contained rather than heroic.

The body is nearly frontal but turns slightly toward viewer-left.

The head tilts slightly downward and toward viewer-left.

One hip may shift subtly, but avoid realistic contrapposto.

FACE:
Give her a small angular porcelain-like face.

Use:
pale cool pink skin,
sharp narrow jaw,
small pointed chin,
short straight nose,
thin dark brows,
narrow almond-shaped eyes,
subtle red or plum eye accents,
small restrained lips.

Expression:
calm,
quiet,
slightly aloof,
mildly melancholic,
dreamlike.

Do not use a smiling anime expression.

Add small round or oval gold-rim glasses sitting delicately on the nose.

HAIR:
Use a short black bob or sculptural chin-length hairstyle.

The hair is built from one or two large smooth geometric masses rather than realistic strands.

Add a subtle dark burgundy or wine-red highlight on the upper surfaces.

Keep the silhouette clean and slightly asymmetrical.

CLOTHING:
Dress the deity in an elaborate layered traditional Chinese robe redesigned through contemporary graphic geometry.

Construct the garment from large flat polygonal planes.

Base layers:
pale icy blue,
light cyan,
periwinkle,
lavender.

Middle layers:
violet,
indigo,
deep blue,
midnight navy.

Accent layers:
large coral-pink and salmon-pink flowing sleeves and ribbon panels.

The upper garment should include:
high structured collar,
short decorative fastening buttons,
a broad cape-like shoulder panel,
subtle embroidered or cloud-pattern ornament,
thin pale cyan edge lines.

Use one large coral-pink ribbon crossing diagonally across the torso.

Let oversized sleeve strips and hanging panels extend dramatically downward and outward.

The fabric should NOT behave realistically.
No small cloth wrinkles.
Instead use:
long triangles,
broad trapezoids,
angular folds,
clean overlapping ribbons,
controlled curved arcs.

LOWER ROBE:
The lower garment should extend almost to the rooftops.

Use extremely dark navy and black with small blue star-like dots.

Allow parts of the lower robe to become semi-transparent, blending visually into the night sky and city atmosphere.

Inside the lower garment, include long decorative vertical textile panels in:
violet,
blue,
turquoise,
and muted purple.

Add small woven patterns, traditional geometric motifs and long tassel ornaments.

Keep all details highly organized.

LEFT ARM AND GESTURE:
The arm on viewer-left rises upward and outward.

The elbow bends gently.

The wrist turns upward.

The long pale fingers form a delicate theatrical or ritual hand gesture:
index and middle fingers slightly extended,
other fingers relaxed,
palm facing upward.

The pose should feel elegant and ceremonial.

Do not make the hand anatomically chunky.

RIGHT ARM AND LANTERN:
The viewer-right arm extends horizontally away from the body.

The wrist bends gently downward or outward.

The deity holds a very long, thin coral or dark-red rod between delicate fingers.

At the rod's far viewer-right end hangs an ornate traditional Chinese lantern.

LANTERN STRUCTURE:
The lantern is one of the strongest color focal points.

Use:
small intricate gold mounting ornament at the top,
tiny loop and chain,
warm golden-orange umbrella-like roof,
multi-layered coral, salmon and pink fringe,
long vertical tassels,
translucent pale-pink inner body.

The lower tassels should extend almost straight downward and vary in length.

Add a restrained localized rose-pink glow inside the lantern.

The glow should brighten nearby edges of the deity's hand and sleeve slightly, but should not illuminate the whole scene.

RED ANNOTATION LABELS:
Add several small vertical seal-style labels.

Use:
thin red rectangular outline,
red Chinese vertical characters,
small red square seals.

Place them beside:
the deity,
the lantern,
possibly the background mythological figure.

Keep them secondary and catalog-like.

Do not scatter too many.

MODERN CITY:
Across the bottom 18–22% of the frame, create a miniature modern residential city.

Use multiple low and mid-rise apartment buildings.

The architecture should be simplified into clean flat geometric silhouettes:
balconies,
rectangular windows,
roof structures,
stairs,
external frames.

Colors:
deep cobalt,
navy,
dark ultramarine,
almost black.

Do not render realistic concrete texture.

WINDOW LIGHTS:
A small selection of windows should glow:
muted warm amber,
soft yellow-orange,
tiny warm cream.

Most windows remain dark.

This creates a quiet contrast between human domestic life and the giant supernatural figure.

STREET DETAILS:
Near the lower foreground add tiny graphic details:
street lamps,
small railings,
a bicycle,
rooftop antennas,
balcony silhouettes.

Keep them extremely small.

At lower center, place two or three tiny human figures silhouetted on a rooftop, terrace or open platform.

They may appear to be looking upward at the deity.

This small group should reinforce the extraordinary scale difference.

LIGHTING:
Treat the entire image primarily as graphic color architecture.

GLOBAL NIGHT:
very dark low-intensity cobalt ambient illumination.

MAIN DEITY:
front-facing surfaces use pale cyan, lavender and porcelain pink.
turned planes use violet, cobalt and dark navy.

Do not simulate realistic physical shading.

LANTERN:
localized coral-pink practical light;
very soft small-radius glow;
slight warm contamination on nearest hand and sleeve.

CITY:
tiny warm practical lights inside selected windows and street lamps.

No cinematic rim light.
No broad blue halo around the character.
No strong volumetric atmosphere.
No large bloom effects.

TRANSPARENCY:
Use translucent layering as an important design language.

The large background musician spirit should remain highly transparent.

Selected pieces of the deity's lower robe may also become partially transparent.

Overlapping blue planes should create subtle tonal depth without becoming glass-like or glossy.

COLOR SYSTEM:
dominant:
black,
midnight navy,
ultramarine,
cobalt,
royal blue.

secondary:
cyan,
ice blue,
periwinkle,
lavender,
violet.

major accent:
coral pink,
salmon,
hot pink,
muted magenta.

minor accents:
antique gold,
amber,
warm apartment yellow,
seal red.

STYLE:
T1 flat 2D contemporary Chinese illustration.
New-Chinese editorial poster.
Modern cultural illustration.
Geometric elongated anatomy.
Angular vector-like clothing.
Highly controlled flat color blocking.
Selective translucent layering.
Elegant caricature.
Large negative-space design.
Chinese mythology combined with contemporary urban imagery.
Subtle Art-Deco influence.
Mid-century editorial illustration discipline.
Vintage lithographic print grain.
Restrained screen-print texture.

The artwork should feel designed rather than painted.

MOOD:
mysterious,
quiet,
urban,
dreamlike,
elegant,
poetic,
slightly surreal,
a supernatural being silently passing through an ordinary city night.

Avoid horror.

STRICT STYLE FIDELITY LOCK:
Preserve T1 flat 2D rendering.
Preserve elongated elegant anatomy.
Preserve geometric angular clothing planes.
Preserve huge figure-versus-tiny-city scale contrast.
Preserve deep saturated blue night.
Preserve coral-pink ribbon and lantern focal accents.
Preserve translucent ancient cultural silhouette behind the main figure.
Preserve tiny warm apartment window lights.
Preserve matte printed surface and fine paper grain.

Do not convert into photorealistic human photography.
Do not use realistic skin pores.
Do not use realistic hair strands.
Do not use realistic cloth wrinkles or visible fabric fibers.
Do not use glossy 3D CGI.
Do not turn it into game concept art.
Do not use cinematic live-action lighting.
Do not add realistic urban fog.
Do not add cyberpunk neon signs.
Do not add futuristic holograms.
Do not turn the city into a sci-fi metropolis.
Do not use generic anime facial proportions.
Do not add thick cartoon outlines.
Do not over-render the background.

assets.title: 白羽神弓守护天将
assets.prompt:
Create a highly polished vertical 9:16 contemporary Chinese mythological illustration poster in a sophisticated flat graphic editorial style.

The composition should resemble a modern reinterpretation of a traditional Chinese guardian deity portrait, combining ceremonial symmetry, martial authority, celestial wings, weapons, clouds, symbolic annotations and a restrained printed-paper aesthetic.

OVERALL COMPOSITION:

Use a very strong front-facing central hierarchy.

The divine warrior occupies the middle 60–65% of the frame width and the central 70% of the height.

Keep the body almost perfectly frontal.

The head sits on the vertical center axis.

The shoulders create a wide horizontal visual mass.

Two massive wings expand symmetrically upward and outward behind him.

A flying hawk creates a secondary focal point directly above the head.

The bow forms a sweeping diagonal curve across the lower body.

Clouds and tapered lower legs create a narrow descending vertical ending.

Leave clean negative space around the outer wings and lower margins.

BACKGROUND:

Use a smooth vertical field beginning in medium muted sky blue near the top and gradually transitioning into pale cyan, mint and almost ivory near the bottom.

Keep the background simple and graphic.

Overlay:
fine handmade paper grain,
subtle faded pigment texture,
light vintage lithographic noise,
very faint mottling.

Embed several extremely large Chinese calligraphic or seal-script-like forms into the background at very low opacity.

These characters should function as abstract decorative shapes rather than dominant text.

Scatter tiny pale-yellow and warm-white particles around the figure, especially near the wings.

Do not create magical particle storms.

MAIN FIGURE:

Create one powerful ancient Chinese divine archer floating in the exact center.

Unlike an elongated scholar or elegant deity, this character should have broad heavy heroic proportions:

wide shoulders,
thick upper arms,
compact torso,
strong forearms,
large hands,
large ceremonial armor silhouette.

The legs remain proportionally shorter and visually secondary because the upper-body authority is the main focus.

POSE:

Use an almost perfectly frontal pose.

The torso remains upright.

The chest faces directly toward the viewer.

Both shoulders stay nearly level.

The viewer-left arm bends downward and inward, gripping a long arrow or spear-like projectile.

The viewer-right hand grips the large bow near the lower-right side.

One knee lifts slightly forward while the opposite leg descends, creating subtle movement without breaking the icon-like symmetry.

The pose should feel controlled, solemn and authoritative rather than action-heavy.

FACE:

Give the warrior a strongly stylized masculine face.

Features:
broad angular forehead,
straight heavy black eyebrows,
narrow focused eyes,
long straight nose,
defined cheek planes,
square-to-pointed jaw,
short pointed black beard.

Add slight warm coral shading around the cheeks and nose.

Expression:
stern,
disciplined,
watchful,
slightly severe.

Do not use a smiling or emotional expression.

HAIR AND HEADPIECE:

Use deep black hair gathered into a compact traditional high topknot.

Add two long narrow side locks descending past the shoulders.

Place a small orange-gold ceremonial crown or pointed head ornament centered above the topknot.

The headpiece should use simple geometric lotus- or flame-like shapes.

COSTUME AND ARMOR:

Combine Chinese robe structure with decorative mythological armor.

INNER ROBE:
pale icy blue,
soft cloud-gray,
light cyan.

Add broad pale cloud-shaped motifs across the chest.

COLLAR:
deep slate blue and dark teal layered V-shaped collar.

SHOULDERS:
large ornate shoulder guards in warm orange, copper-gold and coral.

Build them using:
scrolling cloud motifs,
curved decorative hooks,
broad layered plates,
small black hollow spaces for contrast.

Do not use realistic metal texture.

The orange-gold armor should remain matte and graphic.

SLEEVES:
large balloon-like slate-blue sleeves,
simplified into wide faceted shapes.

FOREARMS:
dark teal or near-black bracers,
decorated with restrained hexagonal or geometric motifs,
thin jade-green edge accents.

WAIST:
large structured belt system.

Use a central decorative buckle resembling:
lotus,
flame,
sun,
or stylized beast-mask geometry.

Colors:
orange-gold,
coral,
jade,
turquoise.

The belt should become a strong central focal point.

LOWER GARMENT:

Below the belt, add overlapping armored skirt panels.

Use:
dark blue,
slate blue,
navy,
deep teal.

Include:
scale motifs,
wave motifs,
leaf-shaped overlapping panels,
thin gold and jade borders.

Keep every panel geometric and clean.

Do not use realistic fabric folds.

QUIVER AND ARROWS:

Behind the viewer-left shoulder place a rectangular or slightly fan-shaped quiver.

Fill it with multiple arrows.

Arrow shafts:
warm ochre,
golden brown.

Arrow feathers:
deep red,
burgundy,
black.

The quiver should remain clearly visible behind the white wing.

BOW:

Place a large elegant recurved bow across the lower front of the figure.

The bow curves from the lower viewer-left region toward viewer-right.

Use a slender dark body:
black,
deep brown,
dark green.

Decorative bow tips:
orange-gold,
turquoise,
jade.

Add restrained Chinese scrolling motifs around the handle and ends.

Keep the bowstring thin and clearly visible.

The bow should look ceremonial and mythological rather than realistic military equipment.

ARROW / PROJECTILE:

The viewer-left hand grips one long straight projectile extending diagonally downward.

Use a warm orange-gold shaft.

At the lower end, include tiny pale blue or yellow energy-like accents, but keep these very restrained.

PRIMARY WHITE WINGS:

Behind the warrior create two enormous white feathered wings.

They should be almost symmetrical.

Each wing rises upward from behind the shoulder, bends outward and slightly inward at the tip.

Use layered simplified feathers.

Each feather should look like:
a long smooth pale ivory leaf,
outlined or shaded with pale cyan,
slightly warm cream near the center.

Arrange feathers in clearly separated overlapping rows.

Do not create photorealistic bird plumage.

The wing silhouette should remain clean and graphic.

SECONDARY GOLDEN WINGS:

Behind and below the white wings, add a second broader layer of translucent pale-gold and warm ivory wings.

These wings extend more horizontally.

Use long thin feather-like rays in:
champagne gold,
pale yellow,
cream,
light turquoise.

Keep them semi-transparent and decorative.

They should create an aura-like celestial halo behind the main figure.

HAWK:

Above the deity, centered between the upper wing tips, place a flying hawk or falcon.

Show it in frontal-three-quarter flight.

Its wings are fully spread.

Use:
gray-blue upper wings,
white lower feathers,
charcoal head,
small orange-red brow or facial area,
yellow-orange claws.

The bird should feel alert and sharp.

Keep the anatomy simplified and graphic.

CLOUDS:

Around the lower legs create stylized Chinese auspicious cloud ribbons.

Use:
white,
pale cyan,
mint,
very light coral,
soft gold.

The clouds should form thin flowing S-curves and looping bands.

The lower body gradually disappears into these clouds.

Do not create realistic mist.

RED ANNOTATION LABELS:

Place several small vertical Chinese seal-style labels around the composition.

Position them beside:
hawk,
left wing,
right wing,
bow,
arrow,
lower garment.

Use:
thin red rectangular border,
red vertical characters,
slightly imperfect printed texture.

Add one or two small square red artist seals.

The labels should feel like cultural specimen annotations rather than subtitles.

BOTTOM EDITORIAL BAND:

At the bottom edge, place a restrained horizontal credit strip.

Use:
small Latin serif or sans-serif typography,
Chinese title text,
signature-like script,
tiny secondary credits.

Keep the line delicate and secondary.

STYLE:

T1 flat 2D graphic illustration.
Contemporary Chinese editorial poster.
Modern reinterpretation of traditional deity portraiture.
Geometric flat-color construction.
Clean vector-like edges.
Broad heroic proportions.
Symmetrical icon-like composition.
Decorative Chinese cloud and armor motifs.
Selective translucent overlays.
Limited gradients only for plane separation.
Subtle Art-Deco structural discipline.
Vintage screen-print and lithographic texture.
Matte handmade paper surface.

The image should feel meticulously designed, not digitally painted.

COLOR SYSTEM:

background:
sky blue,
cyan,
pale mint,
ivory.

main costume:
slate blue,
ice blue,
deep teal,
navy,
black.

major ornament:
orange,
copper,
gold,
coral.

wing:
ivory,
white,
pale cyan,
champagne gold.

small accents:
jade,
turquoise,
warm yellow,
seal red.

LIGHTING ARCHITECTURE:

Treat lighting as designed graphic plane separation.

Use a broad diffuse frontal-upper key.

Brightest regions:
face,
white wings,
upper chest,
orange-gold shoulder ornaments.

Midtones:
pale blue robe,
slate sleeves,
golden secondary wings.

Shadows:
deep teal,
navy,
black.

Maintain roughly 2:1 visual contrast.

Do not create realistic cast shadows.

Use only tiny graphic contact or overlap shadows between armor layers and feather rows.

No dramatic rim lighting.

No cinematic backlight.

No HDR shine.

No glossy metal reflections.

The gold ornaments remain warm matte color blocks.

MOOD:

solemn,
celestial,
protective,
authoritative,
mythological,
ceremonial,
majestic,
calm rather than aggressive.

STRICT STYLE FIDELITY LOCK:

Preserve T1 flat 2D illustration.

Preserve front-facing centered symmetry.

Preserve broad powerful heroic anatomy.

Preserve enormous white wings with layered graphic feathers.

Preserve translucent secondary golden wing layer.

Preserve central warrior + upper hawk + lower cloud hierarchy.

Preserve clean geometric armor construction.

Preserve sky-blue-to-mint background.

Preserve orange-gold decorative armor accents.

Preserve red vertical annotation seals.

Preserve matte vintage print surface.

Do not convert the warrior into realistic live action.

Do not generate realistic skin pores.

Do not generate realistic facial hair strands.

Do not create realistic feathers.

Do not create glossy metallic armor.

Do not create realistic fabric fibers.

Do not turn the figure into a Western angel.

Do not add medieval European armor.

Do not use game splash-art rendering.

Do not use realistic fantasy concept-art painting.

Do not create generic anime facial proportions.

Do not add volumetric clouds.

Do not add excessive glowing effects.

assets.title: 金榜执笔的文昌学神
assets.prompt:
Create a highly polished vertical 9:16 contemporary Chinese cultural illustration poster centered on the visual theme of examination, scholarship, artistic study and academic blessing.

The image should resemble a modern graphic reinterpretation of a traditional Chinese scholastic guardian or examination deity, combining ceremonial portrait symmetry, calligraphy, painting tools, red examination scrolls, gold symbolic decoration and contemporary editorial poster design.

OVERALL COMPOSITION

Use an extremely controlled frontal symmetrical composition.

Place one young male scholastic deity exactly on the central vertical axis.

The character occupies approximately the middle 50–55% of the frame width.

Behind him, place one massive red vertical scroll that forms the strongest background rectangle.

Around him, arrange multiple giant brushes as long vertical elements.

The composition should read in five layers:

1. warm golden parchment background;
2. large secondary orange-red scroll panels;
3. central deep red examination banner;
4. seated scholar deity;
5. surrounding suspended writing and painting brushes.

Keep the lower margin relatively open for editorial credits.

BACKGROUND

Use a warm vertical field dominated by:

golden yellow,
amber,
ochre,
pale orange,
burnished warm brown.

The upper background should be slightly brighter and more luminous.

The lower area gradually deepens into burnt orange and dark amber.

Add:
fine handmade-paper grain,
subtle pigment irregularity,
faint aged-paper fibers,
restrained lithographic print noise,
very mild mottling.

Do not use a clean modern digital gradient.

Introduce broad diagonal or curved golden bands moving through the background, but keep them highly transparent.

Scatter numerous very small warm yellow-gold particles throughout the middle region, like floating dust or celebratory sparks.

Do not turn them into fantasy magic effects.

ARCHITECTURAL DISPLAY STRUCTURE

At the top behind the red scroll, create a restrained traditional Chinese ceremonial support structure.

Use long horizontal beams with simplified roof-like upturned ends.

Colors:
dark brown,
warm gold,
muted ochre.

Repeat a softer faded secondary version of the structure in the middle-background layer.

This should evoke examination halls, ancestral halls or ceremonial scholarly displays without becoming realistic architecture.

CENTRAL RED SCROLL

Place one huge vertical rectangular red banner directly behind the deity.

It begins near the upper margin and descends behind the torso.

Use:
deep vermilion,
warm crimson,
subtle orange-red gradient,
faint aged-paper grain.

On the banner place oversized golden Chinese calligraphic characters related to examination or scholarship.

The uppermost character should be extremely large and graphic.

Allow lower characters to be partially obscured by the seated figure.

The lettering should function as monumental visual composition rather than ordinary typography.

Keep the golden calligraphy matte and printed, not metallic or glowing.

SECONDARY SCROLL PANELS

Behind the central red banner, add two broad translucent orange-red vertical panels.

These extend lower than the main banner and form a secondary symmetrical architectural shape.

Use muted orange, sienna and warm red.

Their opacity remains low enough that the figure and brushes dominate.

MAIN SCHOLASTIC DEITY

Create one youthful Chinese male academic deity seated in front of the red banner.

BODY

Use stylized but balanced proportions.

The body should not be extremely slender like the wandering scholar series and not broad like a warrior.

Use:

moderately wide shoulders,
narrow waist,
long elegant forearms,
slightly oversized sleeves,
compact seated silhouette.

POSE

Face the body directly forward.

Keep shoulders almost perfectly horizontal.

Sit in a highly stylized cross-legged or suspended meditation-like posture.

Both knees rise outward symmetrically.

The lower legs tuck inward.

The character appears almost floating above a narrow vertical architectural or textile base.

Both arms extend outward at approximately chest-to-waist height.

The elbows bend slightly.

The wrists turn upward.

The fingers perform refined scholarly gestures.

Each side may interact with a thin brush or writing tool.

The pose should communicate:

confidence,
ease,
mastery,
academic blessing,
playful intelligence.

Do not make it religiously severe.

FACE

Give him a young elegant angular face.

Use:
narrow oval face,
soft pointed chin,
straight nose,
arched dark eyebrows,
large but restrained stylized eyes,
slight warm coral cheeks,
small smiling mouth.

Expression:
friendly,
confident,
mildly amused,
reassuring.

Avoid exaggerated anime cuteness.

HAIR

Use long straight dark hair falling behind the shoulders.

Mix:
deep charcoal,
black,
gray-blue,
pale cool highlights.

The upper hair is gathered under a compact ceremonial crown.

HEADPIECE

Place a small traditional scholar-deity crown centered at the top of the head.

Use:
gold,
orange,
small teal accents.

Keep it compact and geometrically simplified.

COSTUME

Dress the figure in layered Chinese ceremonial robes redesigned through clean geometric planes.

OUTER ROBE

Dominant:
pale ivory,
light icy blue,
soft blue-gray.

Create broad angular sleeves.

Use strong triangular and trapezoid folds rather than realistic cloth wrinkles.

SHOULDERS

Build pointed structured shoulder elements with:
ivory,
golden yellow,
warm orange edges.

These shoulder pieces should create a lightly ceremonial, almost architectural silhouette.

INNER COLLAR

Use:
pale cream,
muted gray,
light cyan,
thin gold borders.

Add a narrow layered V-shaped collar.

CHEST

Keep the central chest mostly pale ivory.

Add very subtle thin decorative cyan lines and restrained jade details.

BELT

At the waist place a highly ornate symmetrical academic emblem or lotus-like gold ornament.

Use:
gold,
orange,
coral,
jade,
turquoise.

Make it the strongest decorative object on the body.

LOWER TEXTILE PANEL

Below the waist place a dark muted green patterned central panel.

Use extremely subtle traditional cloud, floral or brocade motifs.

Below that, add a narrow gray-brown knotted ribbon or sash.

The long lower robe extends downward into:
cool muted blue,
pale gray,
small warm edge accents.

HANDS AND BRUSHES

Both hands should be elegant and extremely readable.

Viewer-left hand:
palm slightly upward,
fingers relaxed,
holding or controlling a fine writing brush.

Viewer-right hand:
similar mirrored scholarly gesture,
holding another thin brush or calligraphic implement.

Do not make the hands perfectly mechanically mirrored.

Allow slight natural asymmetry.

GIANT BRUSH ARRAY — VIEWER LEFT

Place multiple suspended traditional Chinese brushes on the left side.

Use a mixture of:

one broad flat rectangular brush,
several long thin calligraphy brushes,
one multi-strand fine-line brush.

Handles:
gold,
ochre,
warm yellow.

Brush hairs:
cream,
pale gold,
light brown.

Some extremely long brush hairs should descend almost to the lower third.

Arrange them vertically like ceremonial banners.

GIANT BRUSH ARRAY — VIEWER RIGHT

Create a larger and more varied brush group.

Include:

large flat painting brush,
round soft brush,
long pointed calligraphy brush,
small detail brush,
one large paddle-shaped brush.

Use different handle thicknesses.

Keep all tools elongated vertically.

The brushes should visually resemble ritual pillars surrounding the scholar deity.

Do not make them look like modern stationery products.

RED ANNOTATION SYSTEM

Place multiple small vertical red labels beside the brushes and figure.

Use:
thin red rectangular outline,
small vertical Chinese characters,
slightly irregular vintage print edges.

Labels may reference scholarly and artistic disciplines such as:

水粉,
国画,
油画,
素描,
书法,
创作,
设计.

Keep all labels secondary.

Do not let them overpower the main banner.

Add one or two small square artist seals.

GOLD PARTICLES

Add hundreds of extremely small gold points around the central figure and brushes.

Their density should be highest around the middle body and gradually decrease toward the outer frame.

Keep them subtle.

No large sparks.

No glowing magical orbs.

CENTRAL LOWER SUPPORT

Below the seated figure, create one narrow geometric vertical support or robe extension.

Use:
muted blue,
pale cyan,
ivory side panels.

The lower shape should taper cleanly toward the floor.

Add tiny blue triangular geometric forms at the base.

This creates the illusion that the scholar figure is seated on or emerging from a monumental abstract lectern.

BOTTOM EDITORIAL BAND

Near the bottom margin, place a restrained horizontal line of cultural-art credits.

Use:
small Latin typography,
Chinese characters,
signature-like script,
tiny secondary labels.

Keep this line thin and visually subordinate.

STYLE

T1 flat 2D contemporary Chinese editorial illustration.

New-Chinese cultural poster.

Modern reinterpretation of traditional examination and scholar deity imagery.

Geometric flat-color construction.

Clean vector-like silhouettes.

Angular layered clothing.

Strong frontal symmetry.

Monumental vertical objects.

Restrained decorative Chinese motifs.

Limited soft gradients.

Subtle translucent layers.

Slight Art-Deco structural influence.

Vintage lithographic and screen-print texture.

Matte paper surface.

The result should feel designed and printed rather than digitally painted.

COLOR SYSTEM

background:
golden yellow,
amber,
ochre,
orange,
burnt sienna.

central banner:
vermilion,
deep crimson.

costume:
ivory,
ice blue,
blue-gray,
muted cyan.

secondary:
deep teal,
dark jade,
gray-green.

ornaments:
gold,
orange,
coral,
turquoise.

accents:
seal red,
warm cream.

LIGHTING ARCHITECTURE

Use a broad diffuse frontal-upper key.

The environment is high-key and warm.

Brightest planes:
upper sleeves,
face,
ivory chest,
golden ornament edges.

Medium planes:
cool cyan-gray folds.

Deepest planes:
dark green waist,
small dark hair masses,
burnt orange lower background.

Maintain approximately 2:1 visual contrast.

Do not use realistic cast-shadow physics.

Use only small graphic overlap shadows between robe layers.

Gold decorations remain flat warm matte shapes.

No glossy metallic highlights.

No dramatic rim lighting.

No cinematic backlight.

No volumetric light rays.

MOOD

auspicious,
scholarly,
warm,
ceremonial,
confident,
youthful,
playful,
academic,
festive but refined.

It should evoke:
examination success,
literary achievement,
art-school entrance examination,
scholarly blessing,
creative mastery.

STRICT STYLE FIDELITY LOCK

Preserve T1 flat 2D graphic rendering.

Preserve frontal symmetrical icon-like composition.

Preserve the central youthful scholar deity.

Preserve large red examination banner.

Preserve oversized gold calligraphy.

Preserve the giant vertical brush array.

Preserve warm gold-orange background.

Preserve pale cyan and ivory clothing.

Preserve red vertical annotation seals.

Preserve matte vintage print texture.

Preserve restrained gradients.

Do not convert into photorealistic historical costume photography.

Do not generate realistic skin pores.

Do not generate realistic hair strands.

Do not create visible realistic cloth fibers.

Do not make the gold photorealistically metallic.

Do not turn the character into a fantasy mage.

Do not add European wizard elements.

Do not create game splash art.

Do not add exaggerated magical energy.

Do not use glossy 3D CGI.

Do not use generic anime facial proportions.

Do not use thick cartoon outlines.

Do not create realistic studio lighting.

assets.title: 春风花伞与奔跑猫群
assets.prompt:
Create a highly polished vertical 9:16 contemporary Chinese spring narrative illustration poster in a sophisticated flat graphic editorial style.

The image should communicate freshness, wind, movement, spring flowers, youthful energy and gentle humor. It should combine traditional Chinese clothing, modern geometric illustration, oversized botanical motifs, a translucent umbrella and playful cats.

The visual identity must remain T1 flat 2D graphic illustration rather than realistic painting or 3D rendering.

OVERALL COMPOSITION:

Build the composition around a strong diagonal motion.

The main female figure moves from lower-right toward upper-left.

Her torso leans slightly forward.

The viewer-left arm reaches outward and upward.

The opposite arm bends inward, holding or gathering long flower stems.

Her robes, hair, ribbons and bouquet all trail toward viewer-right.

The umbrella floats above and to viewer-left, continuing the same diagonal line.

The cats run beneath her, reinforcing the sense of forward movement.

The overall visual flow should read:

upper-left umbrella →
extended hand →
woman's head and torso →
large floral bouquet →
flowing robe and ribbons →
running cats at lower-right.

Do not center the figure rigidly.

Let the body occupy the middle-right region while the extended arm and umbrella open into the large empty upper-left field.

Keep large pale negative space around the top and side margins.

BACKGROUND:

Use a pale warm cream to very light mint field.

The upper background should remain nearly ivory with a faint yellow-green cast.

The lower background gradually shifts into soft mint and pale celadon.

Add:
fine handmade paper grain,
very subtle faded fibers,
light pigment mottling,
restrained lithographic noise,
faint aged-print texture.

Do not create a smooth digital gradient without texture.

Add only a few tiny drifting visual accents:

small pale green leaves,
tiny cream petals,
a few muted orange-yellow petal marks,
faint abstract plant or cloud traces.

Keep the background highly open and airy.

Do not add architecture.

Do not add detailed landscape scenery.

MAIN FEMALE FIGURE:

Create a young Chinese spring goddess, flower maiden or elegant seasonal spirit.

Her body should be slim and elongated.

Use:
small head,
long neck,
narrow shoulders,
long forearms,
long legs,
light narrow torso.

The proportions should feel elegant and slightly exaggerated rather than realistic.

POSE:

The body moves diagonally toward viewer-left.

The upper torso leans subtly forward.

Viewer-left arm:
extended fully outward,
elbow almost straight,
palm open,
fingers splayed delicately,
gesture reaching toward something outside the frame.

Viewer-right arm:
bent inward,
hand close to chest,
holding long green flower stems and bouquet branches.

One leg lifts backward and bends slightly at the knee.

The opposite leg extends down and forward, visible beneath the flowing robe.

The pose should feel like:
running,
floating,
being carried by wind,
or rushing through spring.

Do not make the pose martial.

FACE:

Show the face primarily in left-facing profile.

Use:
slim oval-to-angular face,
small pointed chin,
straight delicate nose,
thin eyebrow,
large but restrained almond eye,
small lips.

Expression:
gentle,
focused,
quiet,
slightly curious.

No exaggerated smile.

No anime chibi expression.

SKIN:

Use pale warm pink or light peach.

Keep the skin perfectly smooth and matte.

Use only simple warm and cool color planes for facial volume.

No pores.

No realistic highlight sheen.

HAIR:

Give her long ash-brown, taupe-brown or muted gray-brown hair.

Part of the hair is gathered loosely behind the head.

Several front strands frame the face.

The majority of the hair streams horizontally toward viewer-right.

Construct the hair using long clean ribbon-like graphic shapes.

Do not draw individual realistic strands.

Decorate the hair with:
small white flowers,
green leaves,
tiny botanical ornaments.

COSTUME:

Dress her in flowing traditional Chinese-inspired robes built from large geometric planes.

UPPER ROBE:

Use:
fresh leaf green,
yellow-green,
pale mint,
sage,
celadon,
light ivory.

The sleeves are very large and dramatic.

Viewer-left sleeve:
opens broadly along the extended arm,
forming long layered triangles and trapezoids,
with bright yellow-green upper sections and darker leaf-green inner planes.

Viewer-right sleeve:
folds inward around the bouquet,
then streams behind the torso.

Avoid realistic cloth wrinkles.

Use only clean graphic folds.

ROBE LAYERS:

Create multiple overlapping garment layers.

Inner layer:
pale mint and ivory.

Middle layer:
sage green and soft jade.

Outer layer:
bright leaf green and yellow-green.

Shadow layer:
deep muted forest green.

Add thin narrow gold or pale yellow piping in selected edges.

Use very restrained decorative motifs such as delicate cloud or floral scroll patterns in the darker green areas.

Do not cover the costume with dense ornament.

RED RIBBONS:

Add one or two long vivid red-orange ribbons.

They begin around the upper torso or waist and extend dramatically toward viewer-right.

Use:
vermilion,
coral red,
deep orange-red.

The ribbons should be narrow, sharp and clean.

They create the main warm visual contrast.

FLOWER BOUQUET:

Create a huge botanical mass behind the woman's shoulders and head.

The bouquet should be almost as large as the torso.

Use many white lilies as the primary flower.

Each lily should have:
large white petals,
pale cream centers,
subtle yellow-green stamens.

Mix with:
small orange-yellow blossoms,
tiny cream flowers,
white buds,
fresh green leaves,
long fern-like branches,
rounded leaves,
slender spring stems.

Build the bouquet as a layered decorative silhouette.

The highest branches extend diagonally upward toward viewer-right.

Some flowers overlap the hair.

Some stems pass in front of the upper robe.

The bouquet should feel abundant but carefully organized.

Do not render realistic botanical photography.

Use simplified graphic petals and leaf shapes.

TRANSPARENT UMBRELLA:

Above the woman, place one large umbrella.

Position it toward upper-left.

Tilt it diagonally.

The canopy should be:
nearly white,
pale ice blue,
very light cyan,
slightly translucent.

Show:
visible radial ribs,
simple central shaft,
thin structural spokes.

Keep the transparency subtle and graphic.

Do not make it glossy plastic.

The umbrella handle extends diagonally downward and ends in a curved hook.

Use pale cyan with a darker blue-violet tip.

The umbrella should feel extremely lightweight.

It may appear slightly suspended rather than firmly held.

WIND:

Establish one clear wind direction.

Wind moves from viewer-left/front toward viewer-right.

It affects:

hair,
long sleeves,
ribbons,
flower leaves,
loose petals,
lower robe panels.

All wind-driven elements must follow approximately the same direction.

Do not allow fabric and hair to blow in contradictory directions.

CATS:

At the lower part of the image, add two running stylized cats.

CAT 1:

Place a slim white cat slightly above and behind the second cat.

Show it stretched horizontally in a running leap.

Use:
white body,
pale green-gray shadow planes,
small pink ear interior,
dark green or gray tail tip.

Give it a narrow alert face.

Its legs extend forward and backward.

CAT 2:

Place a plump cream-colored cat in the lower-right foreground.

Use:
cream,
soft beige,
brown facial markings,
dark gray-brown tail.

Give it very large rounded stylized blue eyes.

Expression should feel comedic, surprised or slightly anxious.

Its body is round and short compared with the elegant woman.

Show it running or floating forward with tiny legs stretched underneath.

The contrast between the elegant goddess and funny cats is important.

PARTIAL CROPPED FIGURE:

At the far viewer-left edge, include a cropped fragment of another moving person.

Only show:
part of a dark green robe,
one pale lower leg,
one brown shoe.

Do not show the whole second person.

This partial crop should suggest that the woman and cats are part of a larger moving group beyond the frame.

Keep this element visually secondary.

RED ANNOTATION SEALS:

Place one narrow vertical red annotation label beside the woman's lower-left body.

Use:
thin red rectangular outline,
vertical Chinese characters,
slightly imperfect printed edge.

Add one small square red artist seal below.

Do not overuse annotation labels in this composition.

BOTTOM EDITORIAL BAND:

Near the bottom margin, place a restrained horizontal credit line.

Use:
small Latin typography,
Chinese title lettering,
signature-like script,
tiny secondary marks.

Keep the line subtle and green-gray rather than high contrast.

COMPOSITIONAL RHYTHM:

The umbrella creates the upper-left arc.

The extended arm creates the first long diagonal.

The bouquet forms a circular mass around the head and shoulders.

The woman's robe creates the central flowing body.

Red ribbons cut sharply across the green shapes.

The lower robe and legs descend diagonally.

The cats provide a horizontal lower counter-movement.

The entire picture should feel like one long wind-driven sweep.

STYLE:

T1 flat 2D contemporary Chinese editorial illustration.

New-Chinese cultural poster.

Geometric flat-color construction.

Elegant elongated anatomy.

Graphic simplified facial features.

Large angular robe planes.

Soft organic botanical silhouettes contrasted with angular clothing.

Clean vector-like edge control.

Limited restrained gradients.

Selective translucent umbrella layers.

Subtle Art-Deco compositional discipline.

Vintage Chinese lithographic and screen-print surface.

Matte paper finish.

The artwork should feel designed and printed rather than painted.

COLOR SYSTEM:

background:
warm cream,
pale yellow-green,
mint,
celadon.

costume:
leaf green,
yellow-green,
sage,
jade,
forest green,
ivory.

flowers:
white,
cream,
pale yellow,
muted orange.

skin:
soft peach-pink.

hair:
ash brown,
taupe,
muted charcoal.

accent:
vermilion,
coral red,
orange-red.

umbrella:
white,
ice blue,
pale cyan.

cats:
white,
cream,
beige,
brown,
small blue accents.

LIGHTING ARCHITECTURE:

Use broad diffuse frontal-upper illumination.

Keep the entire image high-key.

Brightest areas:
umbrella,
white lilies,
face,
pale robe panels.

Midtones:
mint and yellow-green costume planes.

Darkest planes:
deep green garment interiors,
dark hair,
cat tail.

Maintain very low contrast, approximately 1.5:1 to 2:1.

Do not create realistic cast shadows.

Only use small graphic overlap shadows between:
robe layers,
flower petals,
hair,
umbrella ribs.

No rim lighting.

No cinematic backlight.

No volumetric fog.

No HDR.

Keep shadows slightly cooler green-gray while highlights remain warm cream and pale cyan.

MOOD:

fresh,
springlike,
light,
poetic,
playful,
gentle,
wind-swept,
optimistic,
youthful.

STRICT STYLE FIDELITY LOCK:

Preserve T1 flat 2D illustration.

Preserve diagonal running / floating composition.

Preserve pale cream-and-mint negative space.

Preserve giant floral bouquet.

Preserve transparent blue-white umbrella.

Preserve elongated green layered robes.

Preserve vivid red ribbons.

Preserve two stylized running cats.

Preserve handmade paper grain.

Preserve restrained gradients.

Do not convert into photorealistic costume photography.

Do not use realistic skin pores.

Do not use realistic hair strands.

Do not generate realistic flower photography.

Do not create realistic umbrella reflections.

Do not render glossy 3D CGI.

Do not turn the woman into a generic anime heroine.

Do not add magical glowing particles.

Do not add fantasy castle or landscape.

Do not add dense background scenery.

Do not use thick black cartoon outlines.

Do not make the colors neon.

assets.title: 赤豹镇枝与骨戟神守
assets.prompt:
Create a highly polished vertical 9:16 contemporary Chinese mythological editorial poster in a sophisticated T1 flat 2D graphic illustration style.

The entire image should feel like a modern Chinese cultural poster depicting a sacred leopard guardian, combining exaggerated animal anatomy, ceremonial stillness, calligraphic natural forms, abstract mythological objects and large areas of printed-paper negative space.

The visual identity must remain graphic, flat, geometric and editorial rather than realistic, painterly or 3D.

OVERALL COMPOSITION

Build the poster around one monumental stylized leopard placed slightly left of the central vertical axis.

The composition should be tall, sparse and strongly vertical.

The leopard forms the primary vertical mass.

A tall golden ceremonial weapon forms a second thinner vertical axis immediately to viewer-right.

A twisted dark dead tree expands diagonally across the upper-left and upper-middle.

Layered blue supernatural rock-cloud forms anchor the lower half.

A long curled tail closes the lower-right composition.

Leave very large areas of empty pink background around the subject, especially:
upper-right,
far-left,
outer margins,
and lower side regions.

The image should feel deliberately designed rather than filled.

MAIN SUBJECT — LEOPARD

The central creature is a LEOPARD.

It must remain unmistakably feline.

Do not interpret the unusual proportions as giraffe anatomy.

The leopard has been mythologically elongated and graphically stylized, but every essential structural cue remains feline.

BODY TYPE

Use an exaggerated sacred-animal silhouette:

compact feline head,
short neck,
high vertical chest,
extremely elongated upright torso,
long forelegs,
large folded haunches,
long heavy tail.

The animal is tall because the seated torso is stretched vertically.

The neck itself remains short.

Do not create a long-necked silhouette.

POSE

The leopard is sitting upright on its haunches like a monumental ceremonial guardian statue.

Show the body mainly in viewer-left-facing side profile, with only a very slight three-quarter opening so that the chest and both forelegs remain readable.

The pelvis and rear body sit low near the ground.

The chest rises almost vertically from the pelvis.

The spine forms a tall upright line rather than a horizontal quadruped back.

The posture should feel:
still,
ritualistic,
proud,
slightly surreal,
highly controlled.

Do not create any active movement.

HEAD ORIENTATION

The head sits high but directly above a short feline neck.

Turn the head toward viewer-left.

Tilt the muzzle slightly upward toward upper-left.

Lift the chin subtly.

The animal should appear to look outward into the distance rather than down toward the ground.

Keep the expression aloof and sacred.

HEAD STRUCTURE

Design an unmistakable stylized leopard head.

Use:

broad wedge-shaped feline forehead,
compact skull,
small rounded-triangular ears,
short broad muzzle,
dark compact feline nose,
strong cheek planes,
defined jawline,
narrow almond-shaped predator eye.

The eye should angle slightly upward at the outer corner.

Use a pale ivory-white area across the cheek, muzzle underside and lower jaw.

Add a distinct long dark throat ornament directly beneath the chin.

This shape can resemble:
a stylized black beard,
a mane-like throat tuft,
or a ceremonial graphic fur mass.

It must remain a decorative feline feature, not a horse beard or goat beard.

Do not add:
antlers,
horns,
ossicones,
long equine ears,
deer muzzle,
horse muzzle,
giraffe muzzle.

NECK

The neck is short relative to the body.

Use a compact thick feline neck connecting the jaw directly into the high chest.

Allow only a very slight backward curve.

Do not separate the head from the torso using a long narrow stalk.

The apparent height must come from the torso.

TORSO

Stretch the chest and abdomen vertically.

The torso should feel narrow and architectural.

Use:

high chest,
slender abdomen,
slightly tucked belly,
narrow waist,
compact rump.

The shoulder mass should remain feline but simplified.

Do not use the deep horizontal barrel body of a horse.

Do not use the sloping torso of a giraffe.

Do not create a dog-like ribcage.

FORELEGS

Both forelegs are clearly visible.

They descend almost vertically from the chest.

Position them very close together.

They should form two long parallel graphic columns.

Keep them:
straight,
slender,
calm,
weight-bearing.

Both forepaws rest on the exact same ground level.

No raised paw.

No stepping motion.

No bent running pose.

HIND LEGS

The hind legs are essential to the pose.

Both rear legs are folded deeply because the leopard is sitting.

Create two large bent haunch masses near the base of the torso.

The upper thighs push slightly outward.

The knees bend strongly.

The lower hind legs fold inward and downward.

The hind paws remain close to the body and near the ground.

The rear legs must never look like two additional straight standing legs.

This is a seated leopard.

The pelvis rests low.

The haunches carry the rear body weight.

PAWS

All paws are simplified feline paws.

Use broad rounded shapes.

Do not create realistic toe anatomy.

Do not use hooves.

The paw color may shift toward:
pale mint,
icy cyan,
soft blue-green,
cream.

Keep these accents graphic and restrained.

TAIL

Create one long thick leopard tail.

It emerges from the rear haunch.

The tail immediately drops downward.

It lies low along the ground.

It then sweeps horizontally toward viewer-right.

Near the lower-right, it forms one large smooth looping curve.

The final tip returns slightly inward and ends in a dark oversized tuft-like graphic shape.

Use:
coral-red base,
dark burgundy markings,
black or deep wine-colored terminal tuft.

Do not raise the tail high.

Do not create a deer-like upright tail.

Do not create a thin dog tail.

BODY COLOR SYSTEM

Use warm graphic planes.

Main body:
coral red,
warm vermilion,
salmon,
muted orange-red,
soft terracotta.

Light planes:
ivory,
cream,
pale peach,
warm off-white.

Dark markings:
deep burgundy,
dark brown-red,
near-black wine color.

Optional small transitions:
muted olive,
ochre,
dusty yellow-green.

WHITE CHEST PLANE

One of the most important visual features is a broad uninterrupted pale ivory plane.

It begins at the lower muzzle and jaw.

It continues down:
throat,
front neck,
chest,
central underside,
inner forelegs.

This light plane creates the long vertical visual rhythm of the animal.

Keep the pale area broad and clean.

Do not fragment it into tiny fur patches.

LEOPARD MARKINGS

Use large irregular leopard-like graphic markings.

Concentrate them along:

side of head,
outer neck,
shoulder,
side torso,
outer thighs,
legs,
tail.

The markings should be intentionally designed rather than biologically accurate.

Use:
irregular rounded blocks,
elongated dark spots,
small teardrop forms,
abstract feline spotting.

Do not use:
giraffe honeycomb patches,
regular polygon networks,
zebra stripes,
tiger stripes,
deer spots.

The markings should still read immediately as leopard-inspired.

SURFACE

The animal surface is matte and printed.

No realistic fur.

No hair fibers.

No shiny skin.

No realistic subsurface scattering.

Use only:
flat planes,
subtle paper grain,
very restrained internal gradient transitions.

DEAD TREE

Behind the leopard, place one enormous bare dead tree.

The trunk begins near the lower-middle behind the body.

It bends diagonally upward toward viewer-left.

Then it twists back toward the upper-center.

The branches explode into long jagged forms across the top half.

Use:
deep indigo,
midnight navy,
blue-black,
small cobalt accents.

The tree should feel like calligraphy.

Branches should resemble:
sharp ink strokes,
lightning,
broken brush lines.

Keep them thin, angular and expressive.

Do not add leaves.

Do not add realistic bark.

Do not create natural tree texture.

CEREMONIAL POLEARM

On viewer-right of the leopard, place one extremely tall slender mythological ceremonial weapon.

The shaft begins near the lower ground and rises almost vertically.

Use:
warm pale gold,
ochre,
soft orange-gold,
cream-yellow.

Keep the shaft extremely thin and elegant.

UPPER WEAPON STRUCTURE

The upper section should be unusual and symbolic.

Build it around one long central spear point.

Below the point, add an elaborate openwork structure resembling:

rib bones,
fish bones,
vertebrae,
curved blade ribs,
skeletal ornamental hooks.

The structure should be narrow and vertical.

Use repeated curved elements attached to the central shaft.

Avoid making it bulky.

The weapon should feel:
ritualistic,
ancient,
slightly eerie,
ceremonial.

Do not turn it into:
a normal spear,
a trident,
a halberd,
a European fantasy weapon,
a giant sword.

Do not use realistic polished metal.

Keep it matte and graphic.

BLUE SUPERNATURAL FORMATIONS

Behind the lower leopard and around the weapon, create irregular layered blue formations.

These forms should feel ambiguous.

They may resemble:
Taihu rock,
supernatural cloud,
mineral,
burned paper,
torn stone,
abstract flame.

Use:

deep navy,
indigo,
royal blue,
cobalt,
dusty blue,
slate cyan,
blue-violet.

Build each formation from several nested flat color regions.

Use irregular openings and holes.

Create torn organic silhouettes.

Some contours should be sharp and jagged.

Others may curl like cloud forms.

Do not render realistic rocks.

Do not add stone texture.

Do not create realistic geological perspective.

PRIMARY BLUE MASS

Place one tall irregular blue mass behind the leopard's viewer-right torso.

It should rise vertically to approximately shoulder height.

Its upper edge may break into asymmetrical organic lobes.

Create multiple internal cutouts so the pink background shows through.

SECONDARY BLUE MASS

At the lower third, spread a wider blue mass horizontally behind the hindquarters and tail.

This lower mass anchors the composition.

Allow some edges to shift slightly toward violet and pink where they visually merge into the background.

SMALL DARK OBJECTS

On the right side of the lower blue formation, place two small rounded dark objects.

They may resemble:
small fruit,
gourds,
ceremonial seeds,
abstract stones.

Use:
dark plum,
black-blue,
deep violet.

Keep them very small.

They are secondary details.

BACKGROUND

The background is an enormous mostly empty pink printed-paper field.

TOP REGION

Use:
strong rose pink,
coral magenta,
warm saturated pink.

MIDDLE REGION

Use:
dusty coral,
soft rose,
warm salmon-pink.

BOTTOM REGION

Use:
pale blush,
light peach-pink,
soft cream-pink.

The tonal transition should be broad and subtle.

Do not create a dramatic gradient.

PAPER TEXTURE

Overlay:
fine handmade paper fibers,
very subtle grain,
faint aged pigment irregularity,
gentle screen-print texture,
small mottled patches,
slight lithographic noise.

Add only a few tiny faded red or orange marks.

Do not add decorative stars.

Do not add magical particles.

Do not add realistic environmental scenery.

NEGATIVE SPACE

Negative space is essential.

Keep the background mostly empty.

Do not fill the upper-right region.

Do not add mountains.

Do not add architecture.

Do not add forests.

Do not add clouds unless abstract and extremely subtle.

The empty pink field should make the animal feel monumental.

RED ANNOTATION LABEL

Place one narrow vertical red Chinese seal-style annotation near the viewer-left side of the leopard's upper body or neck.

Use:
thin rectangular red border,
vertical red Chinese characters,
slightly imperfect printed edge.

Below it place one small square red artist seal.

Keep the labels visually secondary.

BOTTOM EDITORIAL BAND

Along the lower margin, place a restrained horizontal editorial credit strip.

Use:
small Latin typography,
Chinese title text,
signature-like lettering,
small secondary credits.

Keep the typography compact and subordinate.

Do not turn the poster into a typography-heavy layout.

COMPOSITIONAL RHYTHM

The composition should contain four major directional forces:

1. Leopard:
tall central vertical mass.

2. Weapon:
thin parallel vertical line on viewer-right.

3. Dead tree:
sharp upper-left diagonal and horizontal branching rhythm.

4. Tail and blue base:
low horizontal curve closing the bottom.

These four structures should balance one another.

The leopard remains the unmistakable primary focal point.

STYLE

T1 flat 2D contemporary Chinese editorial illustration.

Modern Chinese cultural poster.

Mythological animal portrait.

Stylized leopard guardian.

Geometric flat-color construction.

Sculptural silhouette.

Large controlled shapes.

Clean vector-like edges.

Minimal contour lines.

Sophisticated negative space.

Graphic anatomical exaggeration.

Restrained Art-Deco-like structural organization.

Vintage Chinese lithographic print feeling.

Subtle silkscreen texture.

Matte paper surface.

Limited gradients only for separating major color planes.

The image should feel designed and printed rather than painted.

LIGHTING ARCHITECTURE

Treat illumination as graphic plane separation.

Use one broad diffuse frontal-upper key.

No realistic directional sunlight.

No hard cast shadows.

Brightest planes:
ivory throat,
chest,
inner forelegs,
pale paws,
gold weapon.

Midtones:
coral-red body,
rose background.

Darkest masses:
leopard spots,
throat tuft,
dead tree,
deep blue formations.

Use approximately 2:1 visual contrast.

Do not use strong rim lighting.

Do not use cinematic backlighting.

Do not use volumetric fog.

Do not use bloom.

Do not create realistic glossy reflections.

MOOD

mysterious,
noble,
aloof,
ceremonial,
quiet,
mythological,
slightly strange,
poetic,
elegant,
sacred.

The creature should feel like an ancient guardian or symbolic beast, not a cute animal.

STRICT LEOPARD ANATOMY LOCK

This subject is a leopard.

Preserve unmistakable feline anatomy.

Preserve:

compact feline head,
short feline neck,
short blunt leopard muzzle,
small rounded-triangular feline ears,
narrow predator eyes,
feline cheek structure,
high feline chest,
elongated upright torso,
seated haunches,
straight forelegs,
deeply folded hind legs,
broad feline paws,
long heavy feline tail,
irregular leopard markings.

STRICT POSE LOCK

The leopard is seated upright.

Both front legs are straight and touch the ground.

Both hind legs are bent and folded.

The pelvis sits low.

The chest rises vertically.

The head points slightly upward-left.

The tail stays low and curls across the ground toward viewer-right.

No standing pose.

No walking pose.

No running.

No jumping.

No raised forepaw.

No four-straight-leg stance.

No quadruped walking silhouette.

STRICT NEGATIVE CONSTRAINTS

Do not generate giraffe anatomy.
Do not generate giraffe ossicones.
Do not generate a long giraffe neck.
Do not generate deer anatomy.
Do not generate elk anatomy.
Do not generate antlers.
Do not generate horse anatomy.
Do not generate horse muzzle.
Do not generate hooves.
Do not generate canine anatomy.
Do not create a long herbivore muzzle.
Do not turn the leopard into a realistic wildlife photograph.
Do not add realistic fur.
Do not add realistic whisker micro-detail.
Do not create 3D CGI.

Do not create glossy fantasy rendering.
